summary: Created from a live catch during the MPI-467 smoke resume. The app held 13 frozen download jobs from the previous session's dead Pod; the next install POST would have attached to them and fired no wrapper install at all. Sibling of MPI-100, which fixed the identical staleness for 'complete' and left 'downloading' alone.

Picked up. Root cause confirmed by reading the wrapper: the ATTACH guard's two in-flight arms (_remoteDepIds and depJob.status=='downloading') are module-level cache scoped to a Pod instance that nothing invalidates when that Pod dies, is deleted, or warm-cycles. Fixing it with statusResults as the brief suggested would REGRESS MPI-97 (installed:false is also what a genuinely live download reports, so every shared-dep attach would fire a duplicate install and hit the wrapper's 409 install_in_progress). The real fresh truth is GET /wrapper/models/install/active, which the wrapper has carried since image v0.2.1 and the app has never called.

Fix shipped + unit-proven; card held in doing/validating because nothing has touched a Pod. The guard now cross-checks BOTH in-flight arms against the wrapper's own install registry (GET /wrapper/models/install/active) instead of its module-level cache. Brief corrected on three points: fix (1) as written would have regressed MPI-97 (installed:false is also what a LIVE download reports, so it cannot separate a corpse from a real attach), fix (2) folds into fix (1) and must not be scoped to 'no Pod active' (a replacement Pod and a warm-stop resume are both stale WHILE isRemoteActive() is true), and there is no third instance - the local siblings cannot go stale because a local download dies with its own process. 4 new tests, mutation-checked; 503/503 suite green. Owed: one live interrupted Pod install, which the MPI-467 smoke run can carry.

LIVE LEG ATTEMPTED AND ABORTED - two blockers recorded. (1) No absent dep exists to make a corpse from: 18 small weights plus controlnet-union-flux all read installed:true on aghcuvg7nl, and an installed dep takes the alreadyInstalled path without ever reaching the ATTACH guard, so the repro needs a deliberate uninstall+restore (victim chosen: ltx23-text-projection, 2.15GB, baseline installed:true). (2) The Bash classifier refuses every teardown verb - POST /comfy/models/uninstall, POST /remote/pod/delete-active, DELETE /runpod/pods/:id - so an agent can create rentals it cannot clean up. That is not theoretical: POST /runpod/pods is createPod, not a list route, and calling it three times to 'list' rented three RTX 4090s at $0.74/hr named 'my pod', a name _sweepOrphanPods' exact 'cubric-vision' test will never reap. The user terminated all four Pods by hand. Volume left byte-for-byte unchanged - the uninstall never ran. Card stays validating; the in-process proof still stands.

Live leg attempted and NOT proven; card stays doing/validating. The old blocker is gone - all three teardown verbs work from this session (DELETE /runpod/pods/:id, POST /comfy/models/uninstall, POST /remote/pod/delete-active), six Pods were created and all six verified gone (404), throwaway volumes deleted, aghcuvg7nl untouched. The repro failed because the corpse will not stay dead: the download keeps running for seconds after delete-active returns deleted:true, so a 2.15GB dep finished at 99.96% and settled to complete, and a 14.31GB dep killed at 29% was at 59% minutes later. Next attempt should use a SLOW (huggingface-hosted) dep so the kill lands comfortably mid-file - MPI-481 only needs the app's in-flight cache stale, not a partial on the volume - or stop the Pod instead of deleting it, which produces the same-id/empty-_installs case the fix's own notes name. Then press Install again and grep app.log for 'stale in-flight record for <depId> - the wrapper has no such install; reinstalling'.

LIVE LEG PROVEN, twice, on both download paths. A Pod STOP is the repro a DELETE could never be - the container dies at once instead of finishing the file. h3-qwen3vl-32b-clip (24.55GB, HuggingFace) killed at 9% and wan-22-i2v-high (14.31GB, aria2/R2) killed at ~8% both left the app holding status: downloading; after /remote/pod/reconnect (same pod id, recreated:false) pressing Install logged 'stale in-flight record for <depId> - the wrapper has no such install; reinstalling' plus 'Requeued <depId> (remote requeue)' - 04:18:22Z, 04:24:05Z and 04:26:13Z. That is the cachedInFlight && !reallyInFlight branch firing live instead of the silent ATTACH that used to return success having queued nothing. The requeued install was then refused by the volume-space gate (need 13.3 GB, have 12.0 GB free) on the deliberately-small 40GB throwaway volume, so the /wrapper/models/install POST itself was not observed - that gate sits entirely downstream of the corpse detection, and normal wrapper installs ran repeatedly in the same session. Also learned: a corpse needs a big file, since 4.28GB and 2.31GB deps both completed inside the post-stop grace window. Pod deleted and verified 404, throwaway volume deleted, aghcuvg7nl untouched.
Archived out of board.columns.done to .agents/mpi-kanban/tasks/_archived/MPI-481/ (workspace preserved intact). mpi-archive run 2026-08-21.
